_shape: FINAL STEP, not a team shape. One agent that closes out a finished team.
_why_this_works: Aggregating and correcting other agents' work is only safe AFTER every member is finished: all the evidence exists, nothing is still moving, and there is no authority to send new work. A standing coordinator doing the same jobs mid-run decides with less context than the lead and then acts on it. Run the closer once, at the end, with no power to change the plan. It also turns the whole team's output into ONE wake-up for the lead.
_when_to_skip: A team that wrote no code, such as a survey. Once code exists, the closer runs at every team size, because the lead runs no check itself.
_rules: Launch it only after the LAST wave has finished. Add it to the finished team with `teamwire launch --add`, so its report lands in the same team and archive.

It has NO authority to prompt or correct a member, and `teamwire send` refuses a message from it. It reports; you decide. A closer that starts fixing things is a second implementer with a worse brief.

You act on its findings: triage them, then send each finding that holds to the member that owns it with `teamwire send <team> --to <owner> --type reprompt --file <findings>`, all in one turn. The owner has the evidence in context.
Keep every member open until the closer's findings on it are resolved. `teamwire close <team> --role <role>` removes one member when you are ready.

Its whole job is turning claims into evidence. 'Tests pass' from a member is a claim. It must run each claimed check itself and record the real exit code. A `teamwire verify` PASS is already evidence: teamwire, not a model, ran the check and recorded its exit code with the commit. So the closer runs each command once per commit, the widest one only. In 15 closer runs from 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-06, one check ran up to five times on one commit (labels), member checks ran again on a joined head the full gate had passed (instr), and the same unrelated failures were investigated on each of three branches (ainfix).

Its task class is `judgement`: it judges other agents' work, and a weaker model or a lower effort costs more than it saves here. Run `teamwire models --for judgement` and weigh its sources against each other. Each source ranks only its own entries, so no single rank names the best model. Then pick among the models this harness reaches, at one of the highest effort levels `teamwire models` lists.

It proves tests can fail. For each new test a member claims, and each fix of a finding that a reviewer reported and an owner fixed, it reverts the fix in a temporary clone and confirms the test fails. The clone lives at `"$TEAMWIRE_HOME/cache/closer/$TEAMWIRE_TEAM/clone"`. It is made once with `git clone --quiet <repo>` to that path when the path does not exist yet, and is never a `git worktree add`, the lead's checkout or a member's worktree. For each later check it fetches, checks out the member's branch (detached is fine), and runs `git reset --hard` (which also drops a staged revert) and `git clean -fd` in the clone; without `-x`, `git clean` keeps the ignored target/ and node_modules, so later builds reuse them. When a repository hook refuses either command, it undoes each revert by naming the files it changed, with `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <files>`, and confirms `git status --porcelain` shows none of those files before the next check. When setup made an untracked link or folder that git does not ignore, it adds `-e <path>` to `git clean` for it. Editing that clone is not editing source. Members can have different setups (cargo, bun), and teamwire stores a member's `setup` nowhere the closer can read, so list each member's setup command in the closer's task. It runs each one once in the clone, the first time it checks that member, with the clone's path where the command reads `$1`. That install is allowed, as an exception to the no-installs rule. Never copy target/, node_modules or any build folder from another checkout: each copied file is a new file that the machine's security agent scans, so a copy costs hundreds of thousands of scans. Do not delete the clone; `teamwire close` deletes `$TEAMWIRE_HOME/cache/closer/<team>/`.

It runs the repository's full gate once on each head that ships: each branch that no integrator joins, such as each parallel ticket or a lone implementer's branch, and the joined head, the integrator's branch, when one exists. It records the exit code. On a joined branch the integrator's own check is the full gate, so its verify PASS is that run. The full gate holds each member's check, so the closer runs no member check on the joined head unless the gate leaves that member's tests out. When a full gate fails, it runs only the failing tests on the base commit, once, and does not investigate a test that fails there again.
It must not edit source (the temporary clone aside). Running the repository's test and lint commands is expected; changing code to make them pass is not.
title: Close out CHANGEME

children._note: On Claude Code, give this member the plugins map from the skill's 'Skills and plugins in members', so it reads no other member's findings through memory.
children.title: Verify and integrate reports
children.task: Close out the finished team myteam. Read its comms/ and reports, and `teamwire status myteam` for what each member was asked to do. Members' setup commands: CHANGEME role: command, one per member, from the team's spec files. Then: (1) VERIFY. Run `teamwire verify myteam` once and read every line: it runs each member's check, records the exit code with the commit, and flags edits outside its owned paths and weakened tests. A PASS is evidence for that check at that commit; do not run the same check again on that commit. Then, for every other check a member claimed passed, run that exact command yourself and record the real exit code. A member's 'tests pass' is a claim, not evidence. Skip a claimed command when a passing run on the same commit already holds its tests. Run the repository's full gate (CHANGEME) once on each head that ships: each branch that no integrator joins, and the joined head, the integrator's branch, when one exists. A verify PASS of the integrator's check is that run when its check is the full gate. Do not also run member checks on the joined head unless the full gate leaves their tests out. When a full gate fails, run only its failing tests on the base commit, once; a test that fails there too is not the team's, so report it once and do not investigate it again on a later branch. Wait for a long run with one blocking call, such as `until grep -q EXIT <log>; do sleep 5; done`, not a progress check every turn. For each new test a member claims, and each fix of a finding that a reviewer reported and an owner fixed, revert the fix in a temporary clone at `"$TEAMWIRE_HOME/cache/closer/$TEAMWIRE_TEAM/clone"` and confirm the test fails. Make the clone once with `git clone --quiet <repo>` to that path when it does not exist yet; for each later check, fetch, check out the member's branch there (detached is fine), and run `git reset --hard` (which also drops a staged revert) and `git clean -fd` (no `-x`, so the ignored target/ and node_modules stay and later builds reuse them). When a repository hook refuses either command, do not work around the hook: undo each revert by naming the files you changed, with `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <files>`, then confirm `git status --porcelain` shows none of those files before the next check. When setup made an untracked link or folder that git does not ignore, add `-e <path>` to `git clean` for it. Never `git worktree add`, the lead's checkout or a member's worktree. Editing that clone is not editing source. Members can have different setups (cargo, bun). Run each member's setup command from the list above once in the clone, the first time you check that member: put the clone's path where the command reads `$1`, and run it from the clone's directory. That install is allowed, as an exception to the no-installs rule. Never copy target/, node_modules or any build folder from another checkout: each copied file is a new file that the machine's security agent scans, so a copy costs hundreds of thousands of scans. Do not delete the clone; `teamwire close` deletes `$TEAMWIRE_HOME/cache/closer/<team>/`. If a command cannot run at all, say so; a wrong command in a task has been reported as success before. (2) COMPARE. Name every place two members contradict each other, or where one member's change would break another's assumption. Bugs live between reports, not inside them. (3) CHECK COVERAGE. For each member, say plainly whether it did what its task asked, did part of it, or went off course. Quote file:line evidence. (4) For EVERY finding, name the member that owns it and grade it: 'wrong conclusion' (changes what the team concluded or shipped), 'wrong detail' (a fact or citation is off but the conclusion holds), or 'wording'. The lead routes each finding to its owner by that name. (4b) KNOWN LIMITS. List every `shortcut:` comment the team's branches add, with file:line, as known limits. (5) Write ONE integrated report to your own report file. Start your report file with a summary of at most ten lines: the outcome, then what the lead must decide. Then write what was merged, what is verified, what is claimed but unverified, what conflicts, and what is still broken, most important first. Do NOT edit any source file (the temporary clone aside), do NOT commit, and do NOT message any member. Keep your final chat message to five lines and point at the report.
